title: Ayodhya, the Finale: Science versus Secularism
byline: by Koenraad Elst · Voice of India · 2003 · subtitled The Excavations Debate
lede: Elst's third Ayodhya book is a short one, written as the archaeology finally arrived. In 2003 the Allahabad High Court had a radar survey done, then ordered the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to dig. Elst follows the press coverage week by week. His charge is that newspapers and historians reported “no findings” before the report was out, then explained away the final report. He ends with what a genuinely secular solution would have looked like.

note: Elst writes as a long-standing participant in the Ayodhya debate. The ASI report's interpretation was contested at the time. The Supreme Court relied on it in part in its 2019 judgment, which awarded the site for a temple. This page summarises Elst's account, attributed to him.
